headline: SINDA SILVER SETS TERMS FOR $217M NYSE IPO — ELECTRUM-BACKED GUANAJUATO PROJECT TO PRICE WEEK OF JUNE 29
snippet: Sinda Ltd. (NYSE: SIND), the Electrum Group-backed silver exploration company developing a 182-kilometre mineralised strike corridor across five contiguous concessions in Mexico's Guanajuato silver belt, set terms on June 22 for its US IPO — offering 17.8 million shares at $11.25–$13.25 per share to raise approximately $217 million at a $2.1 billion midpoint market capitalisation. Pricing is expected the week of June 29, 2026, with Morgan Stanley, Scotia Capital, BMO Capital Markets, Canaccord Genuity, Citi, and RBC Capital Markets as joint bookrunners. Sinda is pre-production and pre-revenue — it recorded a net loss of US$18.7 million in 2025 — with proceeds earmarked for infill and exploration drilling, underground access development, and the technical studies required to advance toward a future mine plan. For retail investors tracking the silver capital markets, the Sinda IPO is the largest primary market silver equity offering of 2026 and the first direct vehicle for US retail exposure to the Guanajuato belt, which hosts Endeavour Silver's operational assets and Fresnillo's regional presence — a structural silver-belt entry point entering the market at a moment when silver's sixth consecutive structural supply deficit and China's export licensing restrictions have elevated the strategic value of western-hemisphere silver ounces in the ground.

headline: GENERATION MINING LOCKS IN C$200M FROM CANADA INFRASTRUCTURE BANK — MARATHON COPPER-PALLADIUM MINE CROSSES C$969M FINANCING THRESHOLD
snippet: Generation Mining Limited (TSX: GENM) announced June 22 that the Canada Infrastructure Bank has provided internal credit approval for a CAD $200 million subordinated debt facility — comprising CAD $110 million for development and construction costs and CAD $90 million in standby capacity for cost overruns — to support the Marathon Copper-Palladium Project in Northwestern Ontario. The CIB commitment follows a US$310 million senior debt credit approval announced June 17 from Export Development Canada, ING Capital, and Société Générale, and brings total project financing secured to approximately CAD $969 million, with construction targeted to commence H2 2026. Marathon is one of the largest undeveloped copper-palladium deposits in North America, with palladium exposure providing a distinct revenue stream alongside copper at a time when Section 232 tariff risk makes North American copper projects structurally more attractive to offtake counterparties. For retail investors in TSX-listed advanced copper developers, a combined government-backed and commercial senior-plus-subordinated debt package of nearly C$1 billion — without a concurrent equity dilution event — defines the project financing milestone that clears the last significant construction-go decision obstacle.

headline: GUINEA BANS RAW GOLD EXPORTS — PRESIDENT DOUMBOUYA SHUTS DOWN UNREFINED SHIPMENTS, MANDATES CONAKRY REFINERY
snippet: Guinean President Mamadi Doumbouya announced June 21 an immediate ban on all raw gold exports from Guinea — Africa's sixth-largest gold producer and holder of West Africa's second-largest gold reserves — declaring that gold must henceforth be melted, certified, and refined into ingots at a newly commissioned facility in Conakry before being permitted to leave the country. Operators found exporting unrefined gold will have their licences suspended and mining agreements terminated. Guinea produced approximately 60 tonnes of gold in 2025, the majority of which left the country in dore or raw form. The ban follows similar moves by Tanzania and Uganda and mirrors Ghana's announced trajectory toward a 2030 prohibition on raw gold exports. For western gold producers and streaming companies with Guinean royalty exposure, the refining mandate adds logistics and process complexity to production chains; for investors tracking African resource nationalism trends, Guinea's action under a military-led government signals that the value-capture theme accelerating across the continent is not limited to cobalt or copper jurisdictions.

headline: GOLDMAN SACHS SLASHES 2026 GOLD FORECAST TO $4,900 — $500 CUT AS FED RATE-HIKE RISK PUSHES FIRST CUT TO MARCH 2027
snippet: Goldman Sachs analysts Lina Thomas and Daan Struyven cut the bank's year-end 2026 gold price forecast to $4,900 per ounce from $5,400 on June 21, citing two converging headwinds: the Federal Reserve's removal of its easing bias under Chair Kevin Warsh, with markets now assigning approximately 40% probability to a July 2026 rate hike and 61% probability of two cumulative hikes by December; and the progressive de-escalation of the US-Iran conflict removing the geopolitical risk premium embedded in gold since the January $5,589 all-time high. Goldman's economists simultaneously pushed back their projected Fed rate cuts to June and December 2027, against prior forecasts of December 2026 and March 2027. The bank sees approximately $2 billion in ETF outflows through May 2026 as evidence of investor fatigue. Goldman's revised framework flags $4,440 as the downside scenario if a Fed rate hike materialises and is perceived as more hawkish than warranted by economic data. The $4,900 target maintains a structurally constructive long-term view while acknowledging the tactical headwinds that have driven gold's approximately 25% correction from its January record.

headline: GOLDSEEK COT JUNE 22: SPECULATOR GOLD POSITIONING AFTER FOMC HAWKISH PIVOT — WEEKLY CFTC COMMITMENTS OF TRADERS ANALYSIS
snippet: GoldSeek published its weekly Commitments of Traders analysis for gold, silver, and the US Dollar Index on June 22, covering CFTC positioning data through the June 16 reporting week — the first full data window capturing the shift in speculator positioning following the June 16-17 FOMC meeting under Chair Kevin Warsh, which removed the easing bias and saw nine of 19 dot-plot participants project a rate hike before year-end. The COT report is the primary quantitative tool for retail investors tracking the balance between managed money longs and commercial hedger shorts in gold and silver futures — positioning extremes in either direction historically precede the metal's most significant directional moves. With gold having corrected approximately 25% from the January $5,589 all-time high to the current $4,150-$4,200 range, the June 22 COT data provides the clearest read yet on whether speculator positioning has washed out sufficiently to support a sustainable recovery or remains elevated enough to generate further downside.

headline: GALLOPER GOLD BASECAMP COMPLETE ON GLOVER ISLAND — 7,000-METRE NEWFOUNDLAND GOLD DRILL PROGRAM SET TO BEGIN
snippet: Galloper Gold Corp. (CSE: BOOM) announced June 22 that construction and renovation of the Kettle Pond basecamp on Glover Island in western Newfoundland is approaching completion, clearing the final logistics obstacle before commencement of its 2026 drill program targeting up to 7,000 metres across 25-plus boreholes on the LPSE and Lucky Smoke gold deposits within the Kettle Pond Formation. Glover Island — one of the world's largest freshwater lake islands, located approximately 24 kilometres southeast of Corner Brook — hosts an existing Mineral Resource of 3.1 million tonnes indicated at 1.20 g/t Au and 6.7 million tonnes inferred at 1.02 g/t Au, filed in the 2026 updated MRE. The 2026 program targets along-strike and down-dip extensions of the defined resource. For retail investors tracking small-cap TSX and CSE-listed Newfoundland gold explorers, Glover Island is notable for its year-round road access to a remote island deposit — the infrastructure characteristic that separates prospects requiring multi-year permitting and access investment from projects where drill cost is the primary constraint on resource growth.

headline: NEWMONT CADIA SUSPENDED AGAIN — SECOND EARTHQUAKE IN 9 WEEKS HALTS AUSTRALIA'S LARGEST GOLD-COPPER MINE, SHARES FALL 6.7%
snippet: Underground operations at Newmont's Cadia gold-copper mine in New South Wales, Australia — one of the country's largest producing mines, generating approximately 385,000 ounces of gold and 82,000 tonnes of copper annually and representing approximately 11% of Newmont's net asset value — were suspended on June 19 after a magnitude-3.4 and a magnitude-3.2 earthquake struck the mine site within hours of each other. The suspension is the second in nine weeks: a magnitude-4.5 event on April 14 had already caused a five-week underground halt. No injuries were reported and operations have resumed via a staged restart following surface and underground inspections, but Newmont shares fell 6.7% on the ASX on the announcement as the market processed the compounding seismic risk at its flagship Australian asset. For investors in large-cap gold miners, back-to-back seismic halts at a single asset contributing 11% of NAV create a material geological risk discount that is increasingly difficult to classify as an isolated event.

headline: LINDIAN RESOURCES DRILLS FIRST BLAST PATTERN AT KANGANKUNDE — Q4 2026 RARE EARTH PRODUCTION IN MALAWI ON TRACK WITH 27,000 TONNES ORE ON ROM PAD
source_name: Proactive Investors — Lindian Resources Limited (ASX: LIN)
snippet: Lindian Resources Limited (ASX: LIN) confirmed in its June 2026 operational update that the production drill rig has hit the first blast pattern at the Kangankunde Rare Earths Project in Malawi, with explosives onsite and approximately 27,000 tonnes of ore already stockpiled on the ROM pad — concrete evidence that the fully permitted, fully funded project is leaving the construction phase and entering pre-commissioning ahead of October 2026 front-end commissioning and November 2026 practical completion targets. Kangankunde is one of the world's richest rare earth deposits by contained grade and is the only rare earths project in Malawi — a sub-Saharan African jurisdiction distinct from the Chinese-dominated central African corridor. For ASX and OTC investors tracking western-hemisphere rare earth producers, Lindian's first blast pattern is the operational milestone that distinguishes a construction-stage asset from a production-stage asset, with Q4 2026 now locked in as the first revenue quarter. The timing coincides with China's blacklisting of US-backed rare earth producers MP Materials and USA Rare Earth this month, structurally strengthening the investment case for ex-China rare earth supply.
